sections.content:
Managerial Microeconomics
Utility
monpoly
monopsony
oligopoly
Very, very useful content; the further I learn, the deeper I understand the economics world, and the more I appreciate microeconomics. If you like economics, you will like this course, it's not boring at all.
sections.teaching:
She's extremely responsible to her students, and she will always be ready to answer your questions in class and out of class. You can email her with your questions or see her in her office hour; she's always there. She will arrange office hours before exams and circle key questions that you must understand. She will patiently answer you and provide handwritten sample exam papers before exams.
I will always remember me with other classmates surrounding her, asking her questions one by one; this will forever be a precious university memory buried in my life.
Her teaching is indeed excellent and clear. If you are a student from the mainland, you would be super familiar with this teaching mode. If you are not, trust me, you will like it, though she uses math to explain sometimes, and it could be a bit challenging, but you are guaranteed to learn a lot from her.
sections.grading:
Very generous, she will not fail anyone.
The midterm was a bit higher than the mean, and the final was a bit higher than the mean, ending up with a B+, good enough for the required courses.
sections.workload:
Not demanding.
The essay is very easy, just a real-life observation using the content we learned from class; it's hard to differentiate through this.
Assignments are useful for exams; some exam questions are just similar to homework with numbers changed.
You have to pay a lot of attention in class, she explains the content clearly, and she provides recordings.
Tutorials are also useful; if you want to learn well, you should better attend every class and tutorial.

sections.content: Broad introductory macroeconomic course linked to certain phenomena in Hong Kong's economy.
sections.teaching: Teaching is superb, communicative, creative, and helpful. Professor is willing to discuss any economic questions outside of the syllabus and provide his own insights  on them. The TA, Thomas Au Yeung, however, made plenty of mistakes in marking and ceased to help answer questions or provide valuable economic education on multiple occasions.
sections.grading: Easy if put in the time.
sections.workload: Reasonable and Interesting. No HW required other than readings, and the midterm + finals are pretty straight forward. Project / Presentation induced creativity and enthusiasm as it allowed for creativity and freedom.

Very introductory and simple topics, for example Indifference Curves, Game Theory, Oligopoly, etc.

If you did well in ECON 2113, and is NOT extremely bad in Maths, then no need to worry.
sections.teaching:
Prof. SIU Kam Wing is really nice. He also explains the concepts in a clear manner. He said that he is poor in Maths, so he emphasised understanding instead of calculation.

Besides, he is really talkative and can chat with you after class for more than an hour!
sections.grading:

40% Final Exam

Since both the midterm and final are very easy, everyone got very high marks, so be careful.

In the midterm, one question asked A or B, and the answer is NEITHER A nor B... The TA also told me that you must write down the exact key words professor mentioned in class. That's why I lost some marks even I have pointed out the same idea.

Midterm 94/100, Others unknown → A+
sections.workload: Very light workload. Only 6 problem sets and a 1000-word essay are required to submit via Canvas. The solutions were even posted earlier than the deadlines.

sections.content: The covered materials are a bit more advanced than the Intro MicroEcon and covers a wide variety of topics. But overall, they're still understandable and interesting even for a non-business major like me.
sections.teaching: SIU Kam Wing is generally a nice guy. He's knowledgeable regarding real-world problems and issues but tends to rattle on abt useless stuff sometimes. He's willing to answer questions and often goes off the material to cover more interesting aspects of the topic.
sections.grading: His midterms and finals are essay/problem solving types. So need to really read and analyze his slides because SIU Kam Wing tends to skip lecture slides. I found that having textbook was really helpful for studying.
sections.workload:
8 problem sets from the textbook. There was also a 1000-word essay which was really challenging but fun as you get to explore everyday topics through an economic perspective.

The tutorials just cover problem sets from the textbook, attendance doesn't really make that much of a difference.
